extras.verified_at_basis: re-checked against the first-party page on 2026-11-19 (a verify run); evidence rows dated by the seed pass, which ended 2026-10-21, keep that date as an upper bound
extras.quota_verbatim: S3-compatible storage, slider up to 50 TB on the page; priced at '$100/month ($0.02/GB)' i.e. $20/TB.
extras.limits_verbatim: per-object-cap: none published. Storage at $0.03/10k requests after 1M free. Request pricing exists, unlike Bunny/CacheFly.
extras.egress_verbatim: 'Egress traffic* $0.09/GB — *Charges only apply to traffic outside of our CDN.' So delivery *through CDN77's own CDN* is free; only pulling straight from storage costs. Initial 50 GB egress free, initial 1M requests free.
extras.chaining_verbatim: The free-to-own-CDN egress is the same architectural trick as Bunny and Gcore: keep the origin on CDN77 and never pay egress, because the CDN absorbs it. At $20/TB at rest it is 2x Telnyx and 3x Hetzner, so it only wins if you need 250 TB/month of delivery — which is above the 30 TB target.
extras.tooling_verbatim: S3 API; 'Seamless integration with CDN77 delivery platform'. Growth plan is $990/mo for 250 TB traffic with $3.96/TB overage.
extras.price_verbatim: $20/TB stored; $90/TB egress outside CDN77; $0 egress through CDN77. Growth plan $990/mo for 250 TB delivered (= $3.96/TB).
extras.agent_focus: CDN / edge platforms as storage+egress: Fastly (free tier + Fast Forward OSS), Akamai/Linode, Bunny.net (storage + free origin->CDN transit), KeyCDN, CacheFly, Gcore, CDN77, StackPath status, Edgio/Limelight status, jsDelivr, unpkg, esm.sh, Statically, raw.githack, ghproxy mirrors. Question asked: which CDN gives free or near-free egress so a cheap origin becomes viable. Cloudflare R2 excluded per brief. Hard-probed every per-file cap with real GETs this session.
